deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 78-79): u is a 'Fredholm operator' (trace-class / nuclear operator) on a Hilbert space E. alpha_n(u) = Tr Lambda^n u are the coefficients of the Fredholm determinant det(1+zu) = sum alpha_n(u) z^n. The previous page proved |alpha_n(u)| <= ||Lambda^n u||_1 = alpha_n(|u|), with |u| = sqrt(u*u). It also stated Theorem 2: det(1+u) = prod(1+lambda_i) over the eigenvalues repeated by algebraic multiplicity. Hence det(1+zu) = prod(1+z lambda_i) is entire of genus 0, and, comparing coefficients of z, Tr u = sum lambda_i (formula 23). In modern terms this is exactly Lidskii's theorem (1959) together with the product formula for the Fredholm determinant.

This page is the proof of Theorem 2, in three steps.

(1) Weyl-type estimate: sum |z_i| <= ||u||_1 for any finitely many eigenvalues z_1..z_n with eigenvectors x_1..x_n. Let p be the orthogonal projector onto V = span(x_i). V is u-invariant, so Tr(pu) = Tr(u|_V) = z_1+...+z_n (Schur triangular form on V). Then |Tr pu| <= ||pu||_1 <= ||p|| ||u||_1 = ||u||_1. So the inverse zeros z_i of det(1-zu) form a summable sequence.

(2) Complex-analytic step. The coefficients of det(1-zu) are dominated in modulus, term by term, by those of det(1+zh), h = |u|. Grothendieck invokes the principle: an entire function whose inverse zeros form a summable sequence, and whose Taylor coefficients are dominated in modulus by those of a genus-0 entire function, is itself of genus 0. Together with Hadamard factorization this gives det(1+zu) = prod(1+z lambda_i).

(3) It remains to show that det(1+zh) has genus 0 for h positive hermitian. Write h = sum lambda_i (e_i-bar tensor e_i) with (e_i) orthonormal. Expanding Lambda^n multilinearly, only terms with distinct indices survive. Grouping permutations gives alpha_n(h) = sum_{i1<...<in} lambda_{i1}...lambda_{in}, the elementary symmetric functions. Hence det(1+zh) = prod(1+z lambda_i), a genus-0 canonical product. The whole page is struck through, presumably because it was rewritten elsewhere.

The structure 'Weyl inequality + coefficient domination by det(1+z|u|) + Hadamard factorization, excluding the exponential factor by a growth argument' is essentially the complex-analytic proof of Lidskii's theorem later popularized (e.g. in B. Simon's 'Trace ideals'), here dated 1953.
errors: As transcribed, '|z_1 ... z_n| = |Tr pu|' is wrong. The image suggests a sum, and Tr(pu) = sum z_i (signed), not sum |z_i|. To get sum |z_i| <= ||u||_1 one must insert a unitary (phase) correction on V, i.e. |sum z_i| alone does not suffice. Alternatively use Schur form plus duality with a contraction. The bound is still true (Weyl's inequality), but the step as written has a gap.

The key lemma (summable inverse zeros + coefficients dominated by those of a genus-0 function implies genus 0) is asserted without proof. The bound gives M_f(r) <= M_g(r) = exp(o(r)), so f has order <= 1 and minimal type. Hadamard then gives f = e^{bz} P(z) with P a genus-0 product. Excluding b != 0 needs a further argument, e.g. indicator theory or minimum-modulus estimates for functions of exponential type 0 (h_P = 0 identically forces Re(b e^{i theta}) <= 0 for all theta, hence b = 0). The lemma is correct, but this is the genuinely nontrivial point of Lidskii's theorem and is left implicit.
Minor: the transcription mixes the sign conventions det(1-zu) and det(1+zu); this is harmless.

ideas.what: For a trace-class operator on Hilbert space, the eigenvalues (with multiplicity) are absolutely summable with sum |lambda_i| <= ||u||_1, proved via the orthogonal projection onto an invariant span of eigenvectors.
ideas.where_published: Produits tensoriels topologiques (Memoirs AMS 1955) / La théorie de Fredholm (Bull. SMF 1956), in some form

ideas.what: Domination of the Fredholm coefficients: |Tr Lambda^n u| <= Tr Lambda^n |u|, hence |det(1+zu)| <= det(1+|z||u|).
ideas.modern_name: Fredholm determinant bound via exterior powers

ideas.what: Product formula det(1+zu) = prod(1+z lambda_i) for every trace-class u on Hilbert space, hence Tr u = sum lambda_i, proved via genus-0 / Hadamard factorization and coefficient domination by det(1+z|u|).
ideas.usually_credited_to: V. B. Lidskii (1959); complex-analytic proof as in Gohberg-Krein, Simon
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's 1956 Fredholm paper proves the trace/product formula for 2/3-nuclear operators on Banach spaces. Whether he published the Hilbert trace-class case is unsure.

ideas.what: For positive hermitian h = sum lambda_i e_i* tensor e_i, Tr Lambda^n h is the n-th elementary symmetric function of the lambda_i.

missed.claim: A 1953 statement and essentially complete proof sketch of the product formula det(1+zu) = prod(1+z lambda_i), hence Tr u = sum lambda_i, for trace-class operators on Hilbert space. That is Lidskii's theorem (1959), six years before Lidskii, by the complex-analytic route that later became the standard proof. The page is struck through, so Grothendieck may have doubted the growth lemma or simply rewritten the argument.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: History of the Lidskii trace formula: the standard account credits Lidskii (1959), and Grothendieck only for the 2/3-nuclear Banach case. If Grothendieck's published texts do not contain the Hilbert trace-class case, this page shows he had (or nearly had) it in 1953. It also isolates the precise analytic lemma that is the crux of all later proofs.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains a recognizable 1953 proof sketch of what is now Lidskii's theorem (1959), using the same strategy later found in the standard literature. Surprise is tempered for three reasons: the key growth lemma is only asserted, the page is struck through, and I am unsure whether Grothendieck stated the Hilbert case in print (his 1956 Fredholm paper covers related ground).
